description: CloudSim Plus is a modern Java framework for modelling, simulating and experimenting with cloud computing infrastructures and application services. It is a fork of CloudSim 3 that was re-engineered to remove code duplication and improve extensibility and accuracy, and it models data centres, hosts, virtual machines, cloudlets, network topologies, power consumption, horizontal and vertical VM scaling, host fault injection and dynamic creation of simulation entities. It started as a partnership between the Instituto de Telecomunicações and Universidade da Beira Interior in Portugal and IFTO in Brazil, with FCT and CAPES funding; the latest release in the git tags is 8.5.7, with 9.0 in development and a Java 25 baseline. Coverage: user-defined virtual cloud data centres without real geographic data. Format and access: Java library on Maven Central and GitHub with documentation and many examples; free of charge under the GPL-3.0 licence. Caveats: like CloudSim it abstracts compute and network, not physical plant such as cooling or electrical supply; results depend on workload traces and policy choices supplied by the user. Simulation uses: capacity planning, optimisation of VM placement and energy, resilience of services under host failures, and scenario testing for data-centre digital twins. Related records: CloudSim is its parent project, iFogSim targets fog and edge computing, and SimGrid is an alternative simulator.
